### HYBE RECORDS ALL-TIME HIGH ANNUAL REVENUE IN 2024

Date of issue : _2025.02.25_ HYBE

![Image 2](https://hybecorp.com/archive/XRLuP2LYAuOGsSsD04piRKxqJVDh7NebdcS0jH7cCBEoolU4z07EIWWmlKyqySsYjkB3tr0EXc5lpbSJJbqRcl1Tb25si19rgLt3DWeuWcEV5wqoZ2mce4iyeMAwMePQ.jpg)

HYBE today reported financial results for the fourth quarter and the fiscal year 2024, surpassing KRW 2 trillion in annual revenue for the second consecutive year, a first in K-pop history. 

For the full year of 2024, revenue soared to an all-time high of KRW 2.2545 trillion, up 4% from the previous year. Operating profit reached KRW 184.8 billion, a 38% YoY decrease. The decline in profitability was primarily attributable to BTS' temporary break, a shift in the artist sales mix due to new debuts, and strategic investments in infrastructure and new growth businesses like Weverse and gaming.

For the quarter ended December 31, 2024, the company posted KRW 725.3 billion in revenue and KRW 65.3 billion in operating profit. 

The company’s annual revenue coming from sales of promotions with direct involvement of artists, including albums, concerts, and commercials, recorded KRW 1.4453 trillion. The concert segment grew 25.6%, more than offsetting the decline in album and streaming revenue. Revenue achieved from indirect involvement of artists, including official merchandise, artist content, and licensing intellectual property, tallied at KRW 809.3 billion, representing a YoY increase of 14.5%.

In 2024, HYBE artists dominated the global album charts. SEVENTEEN proved their presence as the only K-pop artist to sell over 10 million albums annually for two consecutive years. With cumulative album sales of 5.45 million copies, ENHYPEN demonstrated their global presence, ranking 8th on U.S. Top Albums chart according to Luminate's 2024 Year-End Report and 9th on Japan’s Oricon Annual chart 2024. NewJeans sold over 3 million albums, making them the highest-selling female K-pop artists in terms of sales share. BOYNEXTDOOR became a million-selling artist in just a year and a half after their debut. 

HYBE artists based in Korea also recorded a total of 5.2 billion streams globally, hoovering up 3.5% of Spotify’s Top 200 Global chart last year. Solo tracks of BTS members Jin, Jimin, V, and Jung Kook as well as Megan Thee Stallion’s “Neva Play” featuring RM charted on the Billboard Hot 100. LE SSERAFIM entered the Hot 100 with “EASY” and “CRAZY” in the first and second quarters. ILLIT’s “Magnetic” became the first K-pop debut track to enter both the Billboard Hot 100 and the UK Official Singles chart. TWS also enjoyed a successful debut year, with their title track “plot twist” charting on the Billboard Global 200 for 8 weeks and hitting No.1 on Melon’s 2024 Annual Streaming Chart in South Korea.

Artists under HYBE MUSIC GROUP APAC also made triumphant comebacks on the global stage, holding a total of 147 concerts and 25 fan meets. This was especially highlighted through SEVENTEEN, ENHYPEN, and TOMORROW x TOGETHER topping Billboard’s Top 10 Highest-Grossing K-Pop Tours of 2024. In the fourth quarter of 2024, particularly, performance revenue more than doubled year-over-year to KRW 188.9 billion. The company will continue to host more concerts and fan meets this year, diversifying tour stops from the U.S. and Asia to Europe and Latin America. 

HYBE AMERICA also saw notable accomplishments in 2024. Global girl group KATSEYE had the best debut year with their double title track "Touch" spending two weeks on Billboard's Bubbling Under Hot 100 and 13 consecutive weeks on Billboard Global Excl. US chart, which proved that HYBE's K-Pop methodology can be successful in the US music market. BMLG’s artists topped 10 Billboard charts, with Carly Pearce earning her second consecutive Grammy Award nomination. QC Music continued its strong performance with major artists like Quavo, Lil Baby, and Lil Yachty. Lil Baby's “WHAM” debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, and all four of his recent albums have debuted at No. 1 on the chart. HYBE AMERICA’s management arm, SB Projects, strengthened its management capabilities by bringing in Cade Hudson from CAA who managed some of the biggest names including Britney Spears, Usher, Justin Timberlake, Lady Gaga, and Selena Gomez.

In 2025, HYBE anticipates growth in operating profit through the comeback of 21st century icons BTS and steady growth of artists, as well as strengthened artist management capabilities across global offices. HYBE aims to revolutionize the global market with a “multi-home, multi-genre” strategy that combines the company’s profound knowledge of the K-pop system with local cultures. In the U.S., HYBE launched a new boy group project with Grammy-winning producer Ryan Tedder. HYBE LATIN AMERICA will launch a new group for the region this year, tailored to the culture and fandom of the local market. In Japan, YX LABELS (formerly HYBE LABELS JAPAN) will introduce a new generation of J-pop groups to follow in the footsteps of &TEAM.

The company also expects to see an improvement in profitability in Weverse, Supertone, and HYBE IM, which required initial investments to propel mid-to long-term growth. Revenue from Weverse's digital membership will be reflected in performance results beginning in January of this year, after the free trial period ends. HYBE IM will strengthen its publishing lineup with the release of "Architect: Land of Exile," a new title from Bonfire Studios, and a number of in-house developed titles including the mobile puzzle game “Puzzle Seventeen.” Supertone's new product "Supertone Shift" has garnered approximately 350,000 subscribers, and "Supertone Play" is delivering its service to B2B clients as AI chatbots.

**Hybe Co., Ltd.**[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-7) ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):하이브; stylized as **Hybe Corporation**; commonly known as simply **Hybe**) is a South Korean [multinational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation") entertainment company established in 2005 by [Bang Si-hyuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang_Si-hyuk "Bang Si-hyuk") as **Big Hit Entertainment Co., Ltd.**

The company operates as a [record label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label"), [talent agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agency "Talent agency"), music production company, [event management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Event_management "Event management") and concert production company, and music publishing house. It has multiple subsidiaries, including [Big Hit Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music"), Belift Lab, [Source Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_Music "Source Music"), [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment"), KOZ Entertainment, and ADOR, collectively known as Hybe Labels.

History
-------

### 2005–2021: Big Hit Entertainment Co., Ltd.

Big Hit Entertainment was founded on February 1, 2005,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-8) and signed the vocal trio [8Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8Eight "8Eight") in 2007.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:0-9) In 2010, the company signed a contract with [JYP Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment "JYP Entertainment") to jointly manage the boy group [2AM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2AM_(band) "2AM (band)").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:2-10) That year, Bang Si-hyuk signed [RM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RM_(rapper) "RM (rapper)") as the first member of [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS") and launched nationwide auditions to recruit other members for the group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-11) BTS made their debut under Big Hit on June 13, 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-12)

In 2012, the company signed [Lim Jeong-hee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lim_Jeong-hee "Lim Jeong-hee"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:1-13) and formed the girl group [Glam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAM_(band) "GLAM (band)") as a collaboration with [Source Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_Music "Source Music").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-14) The group was active until 2014, when it was disbanded due to a controversy involving one of its members Kim Da-hee. Kim was sentenced to prison after being found guilty of blackmailing actor [Lee Byung-hun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Byung-hun "Lee Byung-hun").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-17)

Following the end of the joint contract between Big Hit and JYP in April 2014, three members of 2AM returned to JYP. [Lee Chang-min](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Chang-min_(singer) "Lee Chang-min (singer)") remained with Big Hit to continue with his solo career and as part of the duo [Homme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homme_(band) "Homme (band)").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:2-10) 8Eight disbanded later that year, after Baek Chan and Joo Hee's contracts with Big Hit ended.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:0-9)

In May 2015, Lim parted ways with the agency, following the expiration of her three-year contract,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:1-13) and [Signal Entertainment Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_Entertainment_Group "Signal Entertainment Group"), a [KOSDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KOSDAQ "KOSDAQ")-listed company specializing in artist management and television production, acquired Big Hit through a [KR₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")6 billion [convertible bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convertible_bond "Convertible bond").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-edaily-18) In early 2016, Big Hit ended their stake relationship with Signal and made a full settlement of the bonds.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-20)

In February 2018, Homme disbanded after member Changmin's contract ended. He left the company to start his own agency, while [Lee Hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Hyun "Lee Hyun") continued on as a solo artist.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Lee_Hyun_now_solo-21) In August, Big Hit and [CJ ENM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CJ_ENM_Entertainment_Division "CJ ENM Entertainment Division") released information stating plans to create a joint entertainment agency, with ownership split 52% to the latter and 48% to the former.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-23) Filed under the name Belift Lab, the agency debuted its first boy group [Enhypen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhypen "Enhypen") in November 2020.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-24) In October, BTS renewed and extended their contract with the agency for seven more years.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-25) Big Hit was voted Best Investment Company of the Year at the 2018 Korea VC Awards in December.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-26)

Big Hit debuted its second male group, [Tomorrow X Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TXT_(band) "TXT (band)") (TXT), in March 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-27) Also that month, former [CBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_business_officer "Chief business officer") Lenzo Yoon was appointed co-CEO alongside Bang.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-28) Yoon would focus on the business components of the company. while Bang's focus would be on creative production.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-29) In July 2019, the company acquired [Source Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_Music "Source Music"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-30) and in August, the video game firm Superb.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-31) Thanks to the [Weverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weverse "Weverse") and Weverse Shop[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-33) apps developed by its subsidiary beNX, Big Hit was named the fourth most innovative company of 2020 worldwide by _[Fast Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_Company "Fast Company")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-34)

In May 2020, Big Hit became the majority shareholder of [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment"). The label would retain its independence; however, its artists would now receive greater financial support and global promotions.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-35) The [Fair Trade Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Trade_Commission_(South_Korea) "Fair Trade Commission (South Korea)") (KFTC) approved the acquisition in October.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-36) Big Hit acquired KOZ Entertainment, a record label founded by rapper [Zico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zico_(rapper) "Zico (rapper)"), the following month.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Benjamin-37)

In January 2021, news media reported that Big Hit and beNX had invested a combined ₩70 billion (US$63 million) in [YG Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YG_Plus "YG Plus"), acquiring a 17.9% stake in the company in a merchandising and distribution deal that would see YG Plus' artists join the Weverse social media and shop platforms.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-38)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-39)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-40)[Naver Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naver_Corporation "Naver Corporation") later invested ₩354.8 billion ($321 million) in beNX, acquiring 49% of the subsidiary. In return, it transferred its [V Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V_Live "V Live") video streaming service to the latter for the development of a new integrated fan community platform. BeNX was eventually renamed Weverse Company Inc. as a result of the deal with Naver.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-KJAD_Naver_benx-41) The merger was approved by the KFTC in May.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-42) On February 17, Big Hit and [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG) announced a strategic partnership between the two companies to collaborate on various music and technology-related endeavors.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-43) At the forefront of the partnership was a joint venture between Big Hit and [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Geffen_A%26M_Records "Interscope Geffen A&M Records"), a UMG flagship label, that will debut a global boy group through a new, [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles")-based label following a global audition program set to air in 2022. Big Hit would be responsible for selecting and training the artists, while UMG would be in charge of music production, global distribution, and marketing.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-44) Additionally, other UMG artists, including [Yungblud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yungblud "Yungblud"), were set to join Weverse, already home to [Gracie Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie_Abrams "Gracie Abrams"), [New Hope Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hope_Club "New Hope Club"), and Alexander 23.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-45) On February 25, Big Hit announced a ₩4 billion ($3.6 million) investment in a Korea-based AI company, Supertone, that specializes in creating hyper-realistic voices using technology.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-46)

### 2021–present: Hybe Corporation, expansions, and investigations

Big Hit announced its rebranding into an entertainment lifestyle platform company under the name Hybe Corporation in March 2021.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-47) The company underwent a complete organizational restructuring, which also saw the recording and management arm of Big Hit Entertainment spun off into an independent label named [Big Hit Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music") under Hybe's new Labels division. The renaming was approved at a shareholders meeting on March 30.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-hybe_presentation-48)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-49) The company relocated to its new headquarters in the Yongsan Trade Center in [Yongsan District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yongsan_District "Yongsan District") on March 22,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-hybe_presentation-48)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-yongsan-3) and the rebrand went into effect on March 31.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-50) Hybe acquired [Scooter Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_Braun "Scooter Braun")'s Ithaca Holdings and all its properties, including SB Projects[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-51) and [Big Machine Label Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records#Imprints "Big Machine Records"), through its subsidiary Hybe America[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Hybe_America-52) in April.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Variety_Ithaca-53)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-54) The corporation invested $950 million (₩1.07 trillion) into the America branch to finance the buyout;[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-55) $1.05 billion was paid to Ithaca shareholders and bondholders.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-56) BH Odyssey Merger Sub, a newly created subsidiary of Hybe America, facilitated the acquisition, and was later dissolved after the deal's finalization.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-KJAD_Ithaca-57)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-58) The Carlyle Group, a minority shareholder and original investor, sold its stake in Ithaca as part of the deal. Braun joined Hybe's board, while [Scott Borchetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Borchetta "Scott Borchetta") retained his position as CEO of Big Machine.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Variety_Ithaca-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-59) That same month, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ named Hybe one of the "100 Most Influential Companies of 2021", under the "Pioneers" section.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-60)

Japanese streaming platform [Showroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showroom_(streaming_service) "Showroom (streaming service)") announced a business and capital partnership with Hybe in May 2021 to improve its domestic services and expand access to Japanese content in South Korea, the United States, and globally.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-61)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-62) Hybe was added to the [MSCI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSCI "MSCI") Korea index on May 12, and the index updated on May 28.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-63) Following a second organizational restructuring, Bang resigned as CEO on July 1 to return his focus to music production. He was replaced by Park Ji-won but retained his position as chairman of the board of directors.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Bang_resigns_CEO-64)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-BSH_resign_MBW-65) In November, Hybe entered into an equity-based partnership with Korean [fintech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_technology "Financial technology") company Dunamu to develop a joint venture [NFT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token "Non-fungible token") business for the creation of digital assets.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-66)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Pulse-67) It acquired a 2.6% stake in the company for ₩500 billion ($423.8 million), while Dunamu received a 5.6% stake in Hybe for ₩700 billion ($590 million).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Pulse-67)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-68) On November 11, Hybe won a [Red Dot Design Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Dot "Red Dot") in the Brands & Communication Design category at the 2021 Red Dot Design Awards for its new [corporate identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_identity "Corporate identity") (CI) design.[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-69)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-70) The establishment of a new music label, ADOR,[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-72) was announced on November 12. [Chief Brand Officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_brand_officer "Chief brand officer") (CBO) [Min Hee-jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Min_Hee-jin "Min Hee-jin") was appointed as its CEO and tasked with overseeing the management of the label's first girl group,[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-73) later announced as [NewJeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NewJeans "NewJeans"), which debuted in July 2022.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-74)

In January 2022, Hybe published a series of "original stories" featuring boy groups BTS, Enhypen, and Tomorrow X Together in collaboration with [Webtoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webtoon_(publisher) "Webtoon (publisher)") and [Wattpad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wattpad "Wattpad") as part of a planned IP expansion.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-75) The BTS comic alone earned over 15 million views within two days of release and was the highest-viewed title ever launched by Webtoon.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-76) In March, _Fast Company_ named Hybe the 11th most innovative company of the year globally on its annual top-50 list[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-77)—ranking first in the Media category[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-78)—while _Time_ included Hybe on its 100 Most Influential Companies list for a second consecutive year.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-79) The company topped the "Leaders" category and was Hybe became the largest shareholder of [SM Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SM_Entertainment "SM Entertainment") in February 2023, after it acquired founder [Lee Soo-man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Soo-man "Lee Soo-man")'s 14.8% stake in the company for approximately ₩422.8 billion.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-85) The company subsequently acquired [Galaxia SM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxia_SM "Galaxia SM")'s 1% stake on March 3.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-86) On March 12, Hybe announced that they no longer planned to own the majority stakes of SM Entertainment, said that the bidding war with [Kakao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakao "Kakao") could "damage shareholder value."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-87) On March 24, Hybe announced that it will sell its entire stake in SM Entertainment to Kakao by accepting its tender offer launched by Kakao.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-88) However, on March 28, Hybe instead sold half of its stakes in SM to Kakao, leaving it only for 8.81%.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-89) On May 27, 2025, Hybe announced it would sell all of its shares in SM Entertainment to [Tencent Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent_Music "Tencent Music").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-90)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-91)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-92)

On May 23, Hybe signed a music distribution deal with Chinese streaming platform, [Tencent Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent_Music "Tencent Music").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-93)

On August 10, Hybe announced its acquisition of the remaining 51.5% stake from CJ ENM in Belift Lab, making it as a wholly-owned subsidiary.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-hybefully-94)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-enhypenbacker-95)

In November, Hybe confirmed the establishment of its [Latin music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_music "Latin music") division, Hybe Latin America, based in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), Los Angeles, and Miami.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On August 27, 2024, Min was removed from her role as CEO of ADOR but remained on the company's board of directors and continued producing for NewJeans. Kim Ju-young, Hybe's Chief Human Resources Officer and a member of the board, assumed the position of ADOR's CEO. Min objected this decision, describing her as a "grave violation of the shareholders' agreement."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-96)

In December, it was revealed that the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) was investigating whether Chairman Bang Si-hyuk had entered into secret shareholder agreements with STIC Investments, Estone Equity Partners, and New Main Equity without informing other shareholders or the financial regulator. These agreements allegedly allowed him to financially benefit misleading other shareholders into believing that Hybe would not pursue an IPO.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-97) On May 28, 2025, the FSS referred Bang Si-hyuk to the prosecution after concluding that the investigation met the threshold for charges.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-98) The following day, searched Hybe's headquarters connection with allegations of insider trading by an employee who allegedly used confidential information to profit from acquiring shares in YG Plus, based on prior of Hybe's planned investment in the company in July 2021.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-99)

On May 28, 2025, Hybe announced the sale of Big Machine Rock to Gebbia Media,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-100) followed the next day by the announcement of establishing a Chinese subsidiary.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-101)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-102)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-103)

Company value and investments
-----------------------------

Big Hit Entertainment initially operated as a private company with Bang Si-hyuk as the largest shareholder of its stock.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:3-104) In March 2017, the Korean mobile gaming company [Netmarble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netmarble_Games "Netmarble Games") acquired the second largest percentage of the company, paying a reported ₩201.4 billion ($191.8 million) for 25.71%[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-105)—its CEO Bang Joon-hyuk, and Bang Si-hyuk are relatives.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-106) In October 2018, private investment firm [STIC Investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STIC_Investments "STIC Investments") received an undisclosed share of Big Hit for an investment of roughly ₩104 billion ($93 million).[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-107)

In 2007, Big Hit had four employees and was near bankruptcy, but Bang was able to keep the company afloat after the local success of [8Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8Eight "8Eight")'s _Without a Heart_ in 2009.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-108) Over the years, its value rose in tandem with the increasing global popularity of its first boy group BTS.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-109) In March 2018, Big Hit's earnings were publicized for the first time. The company reported revenue of ₩92.4 billion ($82 million) and operating profit of ₩32.5 billion ($29 million) for 2017.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-110)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-theinvestor.co.kr-111) Initial estimates valued Big Hit at up to ₩700 billion ($624 million) if entered into an [IPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") that very month, making CEO Bang the richest in the South Korean entertainment business due to his large shareholding position, and leaving him with personal ownership value of roughly ₩350 billion ($314 million).[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-112) By October 2018, the company was valued at more than ₩1 trillion.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-theinvestor.co.kr-111)

Big Hit's success has been attributed to its innovative management style, more like an IT company than an entertainment company, which has become the new standard in the K-pop industry; it includes a wide usage of [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media") to capture people's interest and transform it into sales, the creation of artist-related multimedia content, and the full use of [fandom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fandom "Fandom") energy.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-113)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-114) Financials published in March 2019 for 2018, showed a 132% increase in sales compared to 2017, with Big Hit making approximately ₩214.2 billion ($189.38 million). Operating profit rose 97% to ₩64.1 billion ($56.72 million), while net profit rose 105% to ₩50.2 billion ($44.41 million).[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-115) By June 2019, the company was valued between ₩1.28–2.22 trillion.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-116) As of March 2020, its total value was roughly ₩6 trillion ($5 billion).[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-117) Big Hit commenced plans to go public on May 21, and applied for a pre-IPO consultation with the [Korea Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_Exchange "Korea Exchange"). This is required under South Korean law before a company can file paperwork for an IPO.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-118) One week later, the company filed for a preliminary review of their planned IPO.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-119) On October 15, Big Hit was listed in the [KOSPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KOSPI "KOSPI") index and began trading stocks.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-120)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-121)

Per the company's 2020 annual report, its first since going public, Big Hit recorded net income of ₩86.2 billion ($77.6 million), a 19.1% increase compared to 2019's ₩72.4 billion.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-yonhap-122) Operating profit rose 44.3% to ₩142.4 billion, while sales increased 35.6% to ₩796.3 billion[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-yonhap-122)—bolstered in part by album revenue and various acquisitions—with the company experiencing its best quarterly performance yet in the fourth quarter of 2020.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-BH_2020-123) Though concert revenue decreased in the wake of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_Korea "COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea"), merchandise, fan-club, and online-content revenue increased 53%, 71%, and 66%, respectively.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-BH_2020-123)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-124) In 2021, Big Hit became the first South Korean music agency to surpass the ₩1 trillion ($838 million) benchmark. It recorded annual revenue of ₩1.2 trillion, operating profit of ₩190.3 billion, and net income of ₩141 billion ($118 million).[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-125)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-126)

### Hybe America

Prior to the rebrand, the subsidiary was known as Big Hit America. Following the rebranding, Hybe Corporation bought over all ₩1.7 trillion ($1.5 billion) of Big Hit America's shares, making it a wholly owned subsidiary under the corporation, and it became Hybe America.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-KJAD_Ithaca-57) This was in preparation for Hybe Corporation's acquisition of Ithaca Holdings through Hybe America.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Hybe_America-52) BH Odyssey Merger Sub was created as a subsidiary of Hybe America to facilitate its buyout of Ithaca. Once finalized, Ithaca would become a subsidiary of Hybe America, and BH Odyssey would be dissolved.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-KJAD_Ithaca-57)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-Variety_Ithaca-53) The merger is assumed to have been completed in the first quarter of 2021 per quarterly earning reports published on May 14.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-142)

In July 2021, Yoon and Braun were appointed co-CEOs of Hybe America, and jointly managed US operations. Yoon was responsible for "the localization of Hybe's K-pop business model in the US" and "oversee[ing] the training, production and marketing process through which new talent is discovered" while Braun focused "on solidifying Hybe's presence in the US music industry" and "cementing [the company's] competitiveness in the stateside market." Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) Jaesang Lee, who led the Ithaca acquisition, was made Chief Operations Officer (COO).[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-143)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-BSH_resign_MBW-65) Plans for the launch of a new global girl group in collaboration with Geffen were announced on November 4; auditions closed on November 28.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-NME_2021_briefing-144)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-145) Braun became the sole CEO in January 2023,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-146) subsequently leading the acquisition of the American entertainment company QC Media Holdings in February.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-147)

Controversies
-------------

### Dispute with Min Hee-jin

On April 22, 2024, Hybe requested for [Min Hee-jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Min_Hee-jin "Min Hee-jin"), the CEO of their sub-label ADOR, to step down from her position following an [audit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audit "Audit") of the label amidst accusations of Min attempting to make ADOR independent.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-163)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-164) Min released a statement dismissing those claims and also accused Hybe of overlooking the similarities between [NewJeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NewJeans "NewJeans") and [Illit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illit "Illit"), a girl group that debuted in March 2024 under Hybe's sub-label Belift Lab. In her statement she accused Hybe and Belift of refusing to acknowledge the claims of [Illit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illit "Illit") plagiarizing [NewJeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NewJeans "NewJeans")' image from music to style, which caused confusion online amongst fans.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-165)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-166) The value of Hybe's shares fell by 8.03% following the news.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-167)

Hybe officially reported Min Hee-jin to the police for "breach of trust" on April 24 following evidence retrieved from the audit that she is attempting to gain management of the label. Hybe later released text messages between Min and ADOR's vice CEO listing a series of methods to take control of the label. Hybe has also stated that they plan to meet with the legal representatives of NewJeans' members to discuss providing them with psychological and emotional care to support them for a successful return in the future.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-168)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-169)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:4-170) It was also announced that NewJeans, who are set to release a new single in May, will carry out activities as planned.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-171)

On April 25, seven hours after the report was filed, Min held an emergency press conference to deny the accusations against her. During the conference, she shared text messages exchanged between her, Bang Si-hyuk, and Hybe's CEO Park Ji-won, some of which included Bang mentioning groups outside of Hybe. She accused Hybe of fabricating her words and revealed that she had filed an internal report in the past because the company failed to address her concerns over their treatment of NewJeans and her as a producer, however, this was ignored by the management.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:5-172)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:4-170)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-173) Issues regarding Hybe's leadership also came to light as Min accused Bang of trying to control all of Hybe's sub-labels and removing their uniqueness. Min also stated that she's willing to talk to either Bang or Park but they never agreed.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:5-172)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:4-170)

Hybe requested for ADOR to organize a board meeting on April 30. If the board members refuse to attend, then a request would be filed in court to open a shareholders' meeting for the label. The company also refuted all of Min's claims, additionally stating that she should respond to the audit and promptly step down from her position.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-:4-170)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-174) Following a court case held on May 30, Min's injunction to stop Hybe from exercising their voting rights to dismiss her was accepted. If Hybe were to violate this and fire her, they would have to pay a compensation of [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")20 [billion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1,000,000,000 "1,000,000,000") ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")17.48 million).[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-175)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-176)

On November 20, 2024, Min resigned from all her positions (including the board internal director) at both ADOR and Hybe.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-177)

On January 9, 2025, Chairman Park Jung-kyu of the tech company Davolink alleged in an interview that Min had made efforts to "poach" NewJeans. He also mentioned that there had been previous discussions between him and Min regarding potential investment and the possibility of NewJeans leaving ADOR to sign exclusive contracts with another company.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-178)

### Insider trading

In June 2024, South Korean prosecutors charged three employees of Hybe subsidiaries with [insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_trading "Insider trading"). They were accused of selling shares in the company before BTS members announced they were taking a break on June 14, 2022. Prosecutors stated that the employees acted with prior knowledge of the announcement, enabling them to avoid losses ranging from $24,000 to more than $108,000.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-179)

### Leaked audit documents

On October 24, 2024, Hybe came under scrutiny during a [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(South_Korea) "National Assembly (South Korea)") audit when Representative Min Hyung-bae of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(South_Korea,_2015) "Democratic Party (South Korea, 2015)") questioned the company's COO, Kim Tae-ho, about controversial internal practices. Min revealed an internal Hybe document titled "Weekly Music Industry Report," reportedly spanning around 18,000 pages, which contained derogatory remarks about K-pop idols, unverified rumors, and harsh commentary, with parts of it being leaked online after the hearing. In response, Hybe CEO Lee Jae-sang issued a public apology on October 29, explaining that the document was "a compilation of public opinions and reactions related to K-pop trends and issues," shared with a limited number of executives to analyze market and fan sentiment. He acknowledged that the content was highly inappropriate and unacceptable, adding that Hybe was "reaching out to each agency individually to offer our apologies directly." Lee also apologized to the artists under Hybe who had been criticized as a result of the document.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-180)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-181)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybe_Corporation#cite_note-182)

SEOUL, South Korea (CelebrityAccess) — **Hybe**, the agency and label behind high-profile acts such as **BTS**, announced booming revenue and profits for the first fiscal quarter of 2025.

For Q1 2025, Hybe reported that revenue rose to a record **500.6 billion won** (approximately **$348 million**), while **net profits grew to 55.29 billion won**—an increase of nearly **400% year-on-year**.

The company attributed the successful quarter to the strong performance of its **touring division**, which included tours and one-off events by artists such as **BTS, Enhypen, and Seventeen**, among others.

* * *

### Segment Revenue Highlights

**Artist direct-involvement revenue** led the way for Hybe in Q1 2025, totaling **322.5 billion won**, up **48.6%** year-on-year.

**Recorded music** weighed on results, generating **136.5 billion won** in revenue—a **5.9% decrease** compared to Q1 2024.

Hybe’s **merchandise and fan club operations** were also strong performers. **Licensing and merchandise** revenue reached **106.4 billion won**, up **75.2%** year-on-year, while the **fan club segment** grew **39%** to **30.1 billion won**.

* * *

For the second quarter, Hybe anticipates continued strong results, driven by planned album releases and tours, including **BTS member Jin**, who is slated to release his second solo album, _Echo_, in **March**, followed by a **solo tour in June**.

title: Hybe breaks its first-quarter revenues record with 39% ...
content:
With more than 150 concerts already on the schedule for 2025, Hybe said that it expects this part of its business to accelerate further in the coming months as it “plans to engage with fans in regions with limited prior interaction, such as Europe and Latin America, through tours and festivals”.

Hybe also flagged up a 175% year-on-year increase in merch and licensing revenues to KRW 106.4bn, aided by merch sales on those tours as well as ‘character merchandise’ inspired by some of its acts. [...] Click to share on Bluesky (Opens in new window)Bluesky

Hybe breaks its first-quarter revenues record with 39% growth
=============================================================

![Image 4: Avatar photo](https://musically.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/cropped-stu-80x80.jpg)by[Stuart Dredge](https://musically.com/author/stuartdredge-2/)April 29, 2025 April 29, 2025

![Image 5: j-hope](https://i0.wp.com/musically.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/j-hope-scaled.jpg?fit=780%2C515&ssl=1)

K-Pop giant Hybe has published its financial results for the first quarter of 2025, setting a new record for its quarterly revenues.

The company generated KRW 500.6bn last quarter ($348.8m at current exchange rates), up 39% year-on-year. Nearly two thirds of those revenues came from ‘sales of promotions with direct involvement of artists’ –that’s album sales, concerts and advertising.

Hybe said that revenues from live performances tripled to KRW 155.2bn in Q1 thanks to tours from BTS’s J-Hope (pictured), Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together, Enhypen and Boynextdoor.

With more than 150 concerts already on the schedule for 2025, Hybe said that it expects this part of its business to accelerate further in the coming months as it “plans to engage with fans in regions with limited prior interaction, such as Europe and Latin America, through tours and festivals”.

Hybe also flagged up a 175% year-on-year increase in merch and licensing revenues to KRW 106.4bn, aided by merch sales on those tours as well as ‘character merchandise’ inspired by some of its acts.

“The company anticipates growth in both revenue and operating profit in the second quarter, as most artists under Hybe Music Group are expected to make comebacks and resume full-fledged activities,” announced Hybe in its financials announcement.

That includes the second solo album from BTS’s Jin, as well as new releases from Seventeen, Enhypen, Boynextdoor and Katseye. Hybe also pointed to its plans to debut new boy-bands in Japan and South Korea in the coming months.

HYBE Corp. transformed K-pop globally through boy band BTS and fan engagement.

© ANTHONY WALLACE —AFP/Getty Images

formerly:Big Hit Entertainment

Date:2005 - present

Headquarters:[Seoul](https://www.britannica.com/place/Seoul)

Areas Of Involvement:[music](https://www.britannica.com/art/music)[sound recording](https://www.britannica.com/technology/sound-recording)[K-pop](https://www.britannica.com/art/K-pop)

HYBE Corp. is a South Korean global entertainment company established in 2005 by Bang Si-hyuk, an entrepreneur, composer, and [music](https://www.britannica.com/art/music) executive. Founded as Big Hit Entertainment Co., Ltd., the company has grown to become a [multinational corporation](https://www.britannica.com/money/multinational-corporation) with subsidiaries specializing in music production and publishing, talent and event management, and concert production.

Upon its founding, HYBE entered the [K-pop industry](https://www.britannica.com/art/K-pop)—a genre of popular music originating in [South Korea](https://www.britannica.com/place/South-Korea) that blends elements of [pop](https://www.britannica.com/art/popular-music), [hip-hop](https://www.britannica.com/art/hip-hop), [rhythm and blues](https://www.britannica.com/art/rhythm-and-blues), and [electronic music](https://www.britannica.com/art/electronic-music). It competed directly with the big three K-pop producers at the time: SM Entertainment, YG Entertainment, and JYP Entertainment.

HYBE disrupted common management and production practices in the K-pop industry by engaging fans directly through [social media](https://www.britannica.com/topic/social-media) and diversifying its content beyond music to include webtoons, [games](https://www.britannica.com/technology/online-gaming), and original stories. This differentiated strategy—most evident through its flagship act, [BTS](https://www.britannica.com/topic/BTS)—helped transform the company into a global entertainment [conglomerate](https://www.britannica.com/money/conglomerate-business).

HYBE has been a leader in popularizing K-pop in the U.S. and other Western countries. The company’s embrace of social media and fan-driven content has changed how music is made and shared, helping to bring fans and artists together worldwide.

HYBE’s global operations and business structure
-----------------------------------------------

HYBE Corp. operates from HYBE HQ, its headquarters in [Seoul](https://www.britannica.com/place/Seoul) that houses its core creative and administrative teams, and owns three international subsidiaries:

*   **HYBE America.** The U.S. division, headquartered in [Santa Monica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Santa-Monica), [California](https://www.britannica.com/place/California-state), oversees operations in the [United States](https://www.britannica.com/place/United-States). 
*   **HYBE Music Group APAC.** Based in Seoul, this division oversees all music-related functions in South Korea and Japan, including HYBE Japan, based in [Tokyo](https://www.britannica.com/place/Tokyo). 
*   **HYBE Latin America.** The division focuses on expanding HYBE’s presence in Latin American markets, with offices in [Mexico City](https://www.britannica.com/place/Mexico-City), [Miami](https://www.britannica.com/place/Miami-Florida), and [Los Angeles](https://www.britannica.com/place/Los-Angeles-California).

HYBE’s operations have three pillars:

*   **Labels** includes HYBE’s music and entertainment production division. 
*   **Solutions** supports the company’s labels division by managing performances, [intellectual property](https://www.britannica.com/topic/intellectual-property-law), multimedia content, educational initiatives, and games. 
*   **Platforms** includes technology and [social media](https://www.britannica.com/topic/social-media) sites and apps, namely Weverse, an [e-commerce](https://www.britannica.com/money/e-commerce) website and app that connects fans with artists and sells official merchandise.

HYBE’s top artists and collaborations
-------------------------------------

In South Korea, HYBE’s top acts include the company’s lead group BTS, Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together (TXT), Lee Hyun, and the boy band &Team. Among its popular female groups are NewJeans and Le Sserafim.

HYBE America’s top artists have included [Ariana Grande](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ariana-Grande), [Justin Bieber](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Justin-Bieber), and Lil Baby through their association with Scooter Braun’s talent management. Braun became CEO of HYBE America in January 2023. Katseye, one of HYBE America’s earliest signings in collaboration with Geffen Records, marks a significant step in the company’s vision toward creating content that represents an array of cultures.

Big Hit Entertainment: The early years (2005–2012)
--------------------------------------------------

Big Hit Entertainment (Big Hit), the company that evolved into the [global music](https://www.britannica.com/art/global-music) powerhouse known as HYBE Corp., was founded on February 1, 2005, by Bang Si-hyuk, a composer, producer, and hitmaker from record label and production company JYP Entertainment.

The first K-pop act the company signed to gain traction on the South [Korean music](https://www.britannica.com/art/Korean-music) charts was vocal trio 8Eight, which debuted in 2007. The group included singer Lee Hyun, whose solo career continued after 8Eight disbanded seven years later.

In 2010, Big Hit partnered with JYP Entertainment, Bang’s former employer, to comanage 2AM, its second South Korean boy group that would also see widespread success in the K-pop market.

That same year, Bang signed an independent South Korean rapper—Kim Nam-joon, aka Runch Randa (Rap Monster) but better known now as RM—who was part of the underground hip-hop scene. He went on to become the first member of BTS. In its early years, Big Hit faced several challenges, including a scandal in 2012 involving the girl group Glam. Group member Kim Da-hee was sentenced to one year in prison for blackmailing actor Lee Byung-hun. The fallout from the incident led to Glam’s disbandment three years later.

BTS and HYBE’s breakthrough years (2013–2017)
---------------------------------------------

In 2013, Big Hit debuted [BTS](https://www.britannica.com/topic/BTS), its top-billed act and the driving force behind its global success. The group embodied Big Hit’s vision of a new kind of K-pop: Alongside rigorous training and multilingual education, Bang Si-hyuk adopted a less restrictive management style for his artists, especially in songwriting and fan interaction.

By adopting these practices, Big Hit overtook its big three competitors in market capitalization, sales, and global impact, writing the blueprint for modern K-pop success.

In 2014, Big Hit severed its partnership with JYP, losing artists 2AM and 8Eight. The split proved pivotal, allowing Big Hit to focus most of its resources on developing BTS, then still in its early stages of growth.

In 2017, Big Hit made its first foray aimed at international expansion by founding Big Hit Entertainment Japan, through which the company promoted BTS’ The Wings Tour in Japan and the Japanese versions of “Mic Drop,” which reached No. 1 on Billboard Japan’s Top 100, and singles “DNA,” and “Crystal Snow,” both of which made it to Billboard Japan’s Top 20.

Global expansion and acquisitions (2018–2020)
---------------------------------------------

In 2019, BTS released its all-English single, “Dynamite,” which led to the group’s meteoric success in the U.S. and other Western nations. BTS’ triumph in generating international demand allowed Big Hit to expand and eventually diversify its portfolio of assets.

Also in 2019, Big Hit debuted TXT (Tomorrow X Together), its second boy group, further solidifying its position as a leading K-pop agency both domestically and internationally. That same year, it acquired Superb, a game developer specializing in music-based games, and Source Music, a South Korean record label and talent agency. The following year, Big Hit expanded further by acquiring another music label and talent agency, Pledis Entertainment, home to the group Seventeen.

In April 2019, Big Hit established its U.S. headquarters in Santa Monica, California, forming Big Hit America, with [chief executive officer](https://www.britannica.com/money/chief-executive-officer) Yoon Suk-joon and American record executive [Scott Samuel “Scooter” Braun](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Scott-Braun) leading the new subsidiary.

In addition to expanding its influence in the K-pop market, Big Hit’s acquisition highlighted the company’s strategic decision to focus on technologies geared toward interactive fan engagement. This vision was exemplified with the 2019 release of Weverse, an innovative app designed to connect artists with their fans.

In March 2020, _Fast Company_ named Big Hit one of its most innovative companies of the year. Seven months later, the company issued its [IPO](https://www.britannica.com/money/ipo-initial-public-offering) on South Korea’s KOSPI, the country’s main [stock exchange](https://www.britannica.com/money/stock-exchange-finance), achieving a [market capitalization](https://www.britannica.com/money/understanding-market-capitalization) of 8.7 trillion South Korean won ($7.6 billion) by the close of its first trading day.

HYBE’s transformation and restructuring (2021)
----------------------------------------------

In 2021, Big Hit renamed itself HYBE Corp. to better reflect its expansion beyond music and toward a wider range of services. HYBE positioned itself as a global entertainment and media company focused on music, fan engagement, and multimedia content. The name change coincided with a reorganization of the company’s operations into three segments: labels, solutions, and platforms.

Shortly after restructuring, HYBE acquired Ithaca Holdings, a Los Angeles–based media [holding company](https://www.britannica.com/money/holding-company) whose roster included [Justin Bieber](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Justin-Bieber) and [Ariana Grande](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ariana-Grande). The acquisition marked HYBE’s entry into the U.S. market.

Strategic partnerships and innovation (2022–2024)
-------------------------------------------------

In 2022, HYBE inked a deal with [Walt Disney Company](https://www.britannica.com/money/Disney-Company) Asia Pacific to stream original programming on Disney+. The lineup included a BTS concert film from [Los Angeles](https://www.britannica.com/place/Los-Angeles-California), a travel [reality show](https://www.britannica.com/topic/reality-TV) featuring K-pop stars and media celebrities, and a BTS documentary.

HYBE also ventured into [blockchain technology](https://www.britannica.com/money/what-is-blockchain) by launching a [non-fungible token](https://www.britannica.com/topic/non-fungible-token-data) (NFT) project with financial technology (fintech) company Dunamu. The project faced significant challenges, mainly environmental concerns raised by fans and the general public.

In 2023, HYBE kicked off its expansion into [Latin American music](https://www.britannica.com/art/Latin-American-music) by acquiring the label Exile. The move led to the founding of its [Mexico](https://www.britannica.com/place/Mexico)-based subsidiary **HYBE Latin America**, which plans to begin major operations in 2025.

HYBE 2.0: Redefining global growth
----------------------------------

In August 2024, HYBE began a major restructuring to improve its ability to compete globally. Known as HYBE 2.0, the plan aims to broaden its product offerings, tailor its operations to different regions, and pursue other key initiatives.

Under the leadership of CEO Jason Jaesang Lee, HYBE reorganized its operations into three pillars: labels, solutions, and platforms. The labels pillar focuses on the company’s music production and artist management operations, while the solutions and platforms pillars drive the company’s growth in technology and various supporting operations like IP management and merchandising that complement the company’s music business.

HYBE Music Group APAC was formed to manage all music labels in South Korea and Japan. It is also working to establish operations in multiple countries and explore and produce various music styles (beyond K-pop) in local and international markets.

HYBE America, led by Scooter Braun, was given responsibility for developing a management division focused on signing new artists in partnership with Geffen Records. Meanwhile, HYBE Latin America plans to build production studios in Mexico, with operations set to start in 2025.

HYBE America’s signing of Katseye embodies the company’s vision of hybrid cultural production. Based in Los Angeles, Katseye is a “global” K-pop group with six female singers from diverse countries and cultural backgrounds:

*   Sophia Laforteza, from [Manila](https://www.britannica.com/place/Manila), Philippines 
*   Manon Bannerman, born and raised in [Switzerland](https://www.britannica.com/place/Switzerland), with Swiss-Italian and Ghanaian heritage 
*   Daniela Avanzini, an American from [Atlanta](https://www.britannica.com/place/Atlanta-Georgia) of Venezuelan and Cuban descent 
*   Lara Raj, an Indian-American from Los Angeles 
*   Megan Skiendiel, born in [Honolulu](https://www.britannica.com/place/Honolulu), with Chinese-Singaporean heritage 
*   Yoonchae Jeong, from Seoul, South Korea

On the tech front, HYBE’s Weverse is launching a subscription tier in December 2024 featuring several new fan club benefits such as ad-free video streaming, offline storage for on-demand content, and digital currency. HYBE is also continuing investments in [artificial intelligence](https://www.britannica.com/technology/artificial-intelligence) (AI) and [gaming](https://www.britannica.com/technology/online-gaming).

Challenges and controversies
----------------------------

As HYBE has grown into a global entertainment powerhouse, it has faced its share of disputes and criticisms.

One prominent controversy involving HYBE was its clash with its subsidiary Ador, led by CEO Min Hee-jin, the creative force behind Ador’s flagship girl group NewJeans. The dispute revolved around creative and management control, with Ador accusing HYBE of copying the NewJeans concept. The conflict escalated into a bitter, highly publicized legal battle over HYBE’s alleged overreach and Ador’s autonomy as a sub-label.

South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission launched an investigation into HYBE alleging the company falsified documents and omitted information in its mandatory filings. Despite the probe, HYBE was the first K-pop company listed as a major conglomerate by the antitrust regulator.

In 2024, three HYBE employees faced charges for [insider trading](https://www.britannica.com/money/insider-trading). Prosecutors accused the employees of selling HYBE shares in 2022 shortly before BTS publicly announced its hiatus due to mandatory [military service](https://www.britannica.com/topic/armed-force). The news caused HYBE shares to plunge 25%.

Despite these controversies, HYBE has evolved from a regional music production company into a global entertainment leader. By leveraging its K-pop roots, innovative technology, and cross-cultural approach to entertainment, HYBE has redefined how music is created, distributed, and consumed globally.
